newsitem.title: MEXICO: Albright applaudes Mexico's drug crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Albright applaudes Mexico's drug crackdown.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Monday applauded Mexico's measures to crack down on drugs but called for further joint efforts to imprison leading traffickers.

In a speech prepared for delivery to Mexican and U.S. Cabinet ministers, Albright said the two countries had taken "many forward steps" to halt the flow of drugs through Mexico to consumers in the United States.

"But we know that in the struggle between law and outlaw, between democratic integrity and corrupt expediency we are neither winning nor losing, but remain in the hottest stages of battle," Albright said.
Albright was addressing an annual session of the U.S.-Mexican binational commission at a time of troubled relations between the two neighbours over drug issues.

Albright hailed the personal commitment of Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo and his government to uncover drug related corruption and praised steps to stamp out money laundering and ease extradition of traffickers.
But, she said, "we must follow up on last year's high narcotics seizure rates by intensifying joint operations and putting major traffickers behind bars."
Albright also called for fully professional law enforcement institutions and said that personnel must be given "the resources and backing that they deserve."
"We must join in emphasising to all our people, in the words of President Bill Clinton, that 'drugs are wrong; drugs are illegal; and drugs will kill you,'" she said.
Clinton was due to arrive in Mexico City later on Monday for his first official visit to Mexico.

In her address, Albright also touched on the issue of illegal immigrants in the United States, saying that as someone who migrated to that country, she sympathised with those who sought opportunity there.

"But every nation has a right and a need to regulate immigration -- to allow legal immigrants to remain and require those who are not legal to leave. That is our right; but our obligation is to see that in enforcing the law the rights and diginity of every individual -- I repeat, every individual -- are protected," she said.
